Hi Alice — great to hear procurement is lining this up. Quick answers up front:

- Term length: AWS private offers can support multi-year commitments, including 36 months. However, some buyers require annual purchase orders and internal accounting segmentation; we commonly structure a 36-month commitment as either a single private offer with annual invoicing or as three annual renewals tied to the same pricing.
- Pricing/discount: For Redwood, we typically layer a term-based discount: ~10% for 12 months, 18–22% for 24 months, and 25–30% for 36 months depending on commit size and whether Dedicated reserved capacity is included. Final pricing is negotiated per deal.
- Buyer approvals: Commonly the buyer needs (1) internal procurement approval, (2) legal signoff on the PO/Terms, and (3) finance confirmation for budget. The AWS Marketplace private offer flow will also involve the buyer accepting the offer in their AWS Console which is usually done by their AWS account owner or procurement team.

I attached a short checklist and a draft Redwood terms PDF for procurement/legal review (see attachments).

Quick pricing note from the marketplace ops side: when we price a 36-month private offer we evaluate two levers: committed spend discount and capacity reservation (Dedicated). If the customer needs Dedicated GPUs, that pushes the economics (higher minimums) but allows a steeper discount in return for capacity guarantees. For co-sell eligibility we should ensure the listing remains in the right product catalog and confirm the private offer will not block AWS selling motions — Mark, can you confirm?

- Signed FinTechCo procurement form (attached)

Adding recommended commercial structure and a worked example for Alice's team to evaluate: 

Scenario A — 36-month commitment, annual invoicing, no Dedicated GPUs:
- List price baseline: $200k/year
- 36-month term discount target: 28% (net $144k/year)
- AWS marketplace fee and payment pass-throughs unchanged; buyer accepts private offer in their console once we create it
- Buyer approvals expected: Procurement signoff + AWS account owner acceptance

Scenario B — 36-month commitment, Dedicated reserved capacity included:
- Baseline reserved cost: $600k/year (higher), custom discount of 32–35% depending on minimum commit and ramp schedule
- Staggered billing: annual invoices but commitment tracked across term; add SLO/SLA appendix

Operational notes: if buyer expects a single consolidated PO for three years, that can be accommodated, but finance at some customers asks for annual POs tying to budget years — we should be explicit in the offer text to allow either billing cadence and note accounting implications.

Legal comments (high level) before we issue a 36-month private offer:
- We prefer to keep the contract term explicit in the private offer text but allow for annual invoicing schedules; do not conflate billing cadence and term length.
- Long-term offers (36 months) need a clear termination and transition clause if the buyer later wants to exit early — propose a pro-rated termination fee or a 90-day notice with defined unwind costs.
- For co-sell deals, ensure the AWS Marketplace offer references the correct product ID and that we have the right co-sell attach documentation for revenue share tracking.
- SOC 2 evidence: acceptable to provide a consolidated SOC 2 link to the security portal; redwood must provide contact and last inspection date.

I'll prepare a brief SOW Appendix (Appendix A) that captures committed capacity, billing cadence options, and early termination terms. Attaching draft Appendix A for internal review.
